newsitem.title: USA: Spreads on 10-year U.S. swaps could move out.
newsitem.headline: Spreads on 10-year U.S. swaps could move out.

text.p: Though little action is expected this week in the U.S. swaps market, dealers said mortgage market participants could provide a spark to push out spreads at 10 years.
Mortgage portfolio managers are looking to pay fixed rates on swaps. So far, volume is modest, but if the trend picks up, spreads on 10-year swaps would widen, dealers said.
"We're seeing some mortgages shifting short positions into swaps from Treasury hedges," one New York-based trader said.
The 10-year swap sector has been quiet in August. At the close on Monday, dealers quoted 10-year swaps at 34 to 35 basis points bid, 36 to 37 basis points offered.

The week's upcoming Treasury note auctions have added very little spice to the swaps market. In when-issued trading, the upcoming two-year note is yielding slightly more than one basis point more than the on-the-run issue. And at five years, the spread is even less than one basis point.
"Some desks went looking for the new five-year to trade at a big discount ahead of the auction," said a dealer at a European bank in New York.
"They pushed out the spread a week or so ago, but nothing has happened and the spread is back in," the dealer added.
Five-year swaps were quoted late Monday at 27 basis points bid, 29 basis points offered. Spreads on two-year swaps were quoted at 19 basis points bid, 21 basis points offered.
But with little else on tap to move the market, many traders expect a very slow end-of-August week.
"To tell you the truth, my mind is more on the U.S. Open this week than on trading the market," one trader said.
